chatEmpty: Messages from everyone at this table appear here.
needsPlayers: A game needs 5 to 10 players. Invite the group with the room code.
electionBegins: Remember your team, then keep the screen to yourself. The election begins in {seconds} seconds.
chooseEligible: Choose an eligible player to form the government.
voteRecorded: Vote recorded: {vote}. Waiting for the table.
presidentPrivate: Your hand is private. Select one tile to pass the other two.
presidentChoosing: The President is choosing in private.
enactOne: Enact one policy. The other will be discarded.
chancellorChoosing: The Chancellor is choosing in private.
liberalPolicyDescription: This policy does not grant an executive power. The Liberals win when five Liberal policies have been enacted.
liberalVictoryDescription: Enacting the fifth Liberal policy immediately wins the game for the Liberals.
fascistVictoryDescription: Enacting the sixth Fascist policy immediately wins the game for the Fascists.
policyPeek: Policy peek: the President secretly views the top three policies.
investigation: Investigation: the President privately learns one player's party membership.
specialElection: Special election: the President selects the next President.
execution: Execution: the President chooses a player to execute.
policyCountNote: The executive power depends on the player count at the start of this game.
rulesGoal: There are Liberals, Fascists, and one hidden Hitler. Liberals win by enacting 5 Liberal policies or executing Hitler. Fascists win by enacting 6 Fascist policies, or by electing Hitler Chancellor after 3 Fascist policies are already enacted.
rulesRoles: Keep your role private. Fascists know their team; in 5–6 player games Hitler also knows the Fascists. In 7–10 player games, Hitler does not know who the Fascists are. Discussion, bluffing, and deception are part of the game.
rulesNomination: The Presidency moves clockwise among living players. The President nominates an eligible Chancellor. The most recently elected Chancellor cannot be nominated; with more than 5 players, the most recently elected President is also term-limited.
rulesVote: Every living player votes Ja (approve) or Nein (reject) after a nomination. A government needs more Ja than Nein votes to pass. Votes remain hidden until everyone has voted. If it passes, the President and Chancellor legislate; if it fails, the failed-government tracker advances and the next President nominates.
rulesFailed: When three governments in a row are rejected, the top policy of the deck is enacted automatically. This chaos policy grants no executive power, resets the failed-government tracker, and clears term limits for the next election.
rulesLaws: The President privately draws 3 policies, discards 1, and passes 2 to the Chancellor. The Chancellor privately discards 1 and enacts the remaining policy. Policy cards, discards, and claims about them are private—players can tell the truth or lie.
rulesTracks: Liberal policies have no executive power; the fifth Liberal policy wins. Fascist policies can unlock investigation, special election, policy peek, or execution depending on the starting player count. Click any space on either policy track to see its exact effect and whether it has been enacted.
rulesExecutive: Only the current President performs a granted power. Investigation reveals a player’s party, not their exact role. A special election chooses the next President once, then normal rotation resumes. Execution removes that player from the game; executing Hitler immediately gives the Liberals victory.
rulesVeto: After 5 Fascist policies, the Chancellor may request a veto instead of enacting a policy. The President must approve it. If both agree, both policy cards are discarded and the failed-government tracker advances; if the President denies it, the Chancellor must enact one policy.
memoryGoal: Everyone begins with 3 points. Wrong decisions cost a point. At 0 points you become a spectator; the last player still standing wins.
memoryRemember: At the start, memorize every gift and its arrow. After the reveal, opponents’ gifts are face down, but their arrows remain visible.
memoryTurn: If you hold one gift, draw a new one. Pass the drawn gift, or when holding two gifts pass the oldest one, in its arrow’s direction. A double arrow lets you choose left or right.
memoryClaims: Name the gift you are passing. The receiver can accept or call bluff. Accepting a lie costs the receiver a point. Calling bluff costs the giver a point if it was a lie, or the receiver a point if it was true.
profileIntro: Make your player profile, keep your stats together, and get back to playing.
footer: Made for game nights and friendly rivalries.
